IMPLEMENT THIS EXACT APPROVED LESSON CONTENT:

SUBJECT:
Science

GRADE:
Grade 1

LESSSON:
Lesson 5

TITLE:
Materials Around Us 🪵🧱

SUBTITLE:
Learn about common materials, their properties, and why different materials are used to make different objects.

ESTIMATED TIME:
20–25 minutes

==================================================
LEARNING GOALS 🎯
==================================================

By the end of this lesson, the learner should be able to:

• Name common materials such as wood, metal, plastic, glass, paper, fabric, and rubber.
• Describe simple properties of materials.
• Compare materials using words such as hard, soft, smooth, rough, flexible, and waterproof.
• Explain that objects can be made from different materials.
• Choose a suitable material for a simple purpose.
• Understand that some materials can be reused or recycled.

==================================================
OPENING — WHAT ARE THINGS MADE OF? 👀
==================================================

Look around you.

You may see:

🪑 a chair;

✏️ a pencil;

🥤 a cup;

📘 a book;

👕 a shirt;

🪟 a window;

🧸 a toy.

These objects are made from different materials.

A material is what an object is made from.

For example:

A wooden table may be made from wood. 🪵

A spoon may be made from metal. 🥄

A raincoat may be made from waterproof fabric or plastic-like material. 🧥

A window may be made from glass. 🪟

Different materials have different properties.

These properties help us decide which material is useful for a certain job.

==================================================
SECTION 1 — WHAT IS A MATERIAL? 🧱
==================================================

A material is a substance used to make an object.

One object can be made from one material.

Another object can be made from several materials.

For example:

A pencil may contain:

🪵 wood;

✏️ graphite;

🎨 paint;

and sometimes a rubber eraser.

A shoe may contain:

👟 fabric;

rubber;

foam;

and other materials.

So when we study an object, we can ask:

"What is it made of?"

==================================================
VISUAL 1 — OBJECT AND MATERIAL
==================================================

Create a child-friendly comparison chart.

OBJECT → MATERIAL

🪑 Chair → Wood

🥄 Spoon → Metal

🪟 Window → Glass

📄 Notebook page → Paper

👕 Shirt → Fabric

🧸 Rubber ball → Rubber

Caption:

"Objects are made from different materials."

==================================================
SECTION 2 — WOOD 🪵
==================================================

Wood comes from trees.

Wood can be used to make many objects.

Examples:

🪑 chairs;

🚪 doors;

📚 shelves;

✏️ pencils;

🧸 some toys.

Wood is often:

• hard;
• strong;
• easy to shape into useful objects.

Different kinds of wood can feel and look different.

Some wood is smooth.

Some wood feels rough.

==================================================
SECTION 3 — METAL 🔩
==================================================

Metal is used in many everyday objects.

Examples:

🥄 spoons;

🍴 forks;

🔑 keys;

🚲 bicycles;

🔧 tools.

Many metals are:

• hard;
• strong;
• durable.

Some metals can also be shiny.

Some metals can bend when enough force is used.

💡 REMEMBER:

Not every metal object looks the same.

Different metals can have different properties.

==================================================
SECTION 4 — PLASTIC 🧴
==================================================

Plastic is used to make many objects.

Examples:

🧴 bottles;

🧸 toys;

📦 containers;

🪣 buckets.

Plastic can be made in many forms.

Some plastic is:

• hard;

while other plastic is:

• flexible.

Plastic can also be:

• lightweight;
• waterproof;
• easy to shape.

Because plastic lasts a long time, we should use and dispose of it carefully.

==================================================
SECTION 5 — GLASS 🪟
==================================================

Glass is often used when we want light to pass through an object.

Examples:

🪟 windows;

🥛 drinking glasses;

🫙 jars.

Many types of glass are:

• hard;
• smooth;
• transparent.

Transparent means light can pass through so we can see through it.

But glass can break.

Broken glass can be sharp and dangerous.

⚠️ SAFETY:

Do not pick up broken glass.

Tell a trusted adult.

==================================================
SECTION 6 — PAPER 📄
==================================================

Paper is used for:

📚 books;

📝 notebooks;

📰 newspapers;

🎁 wrapping;

🎨 artwork.

Paper is often:

• light;
• thin;
• easy to fold;
• easy to write or draw on.

Paper is not usually a good material for holding water because it can become wet and weak.

==================================================
SECTION 7 — FABRIC 👕
==================================================

Fabric is used to make many things we wear and use.

Examples:

👕 shirts;

👖 pants;

🛏️ blankets;

🧦 socks;

🎒 some bags.

Different fabrics can have different properties.

Some are:

• soft;
• smooth;
• thick;
• thin;
• stretchy.

The type of fabric depends on what the object needs to do.

==================================================
SECTION 8 — RUBBER 🟠
==================================================

Rubber is used in objects that may need to bend, stretch, grip, or bounce.

Examples:

🏀 balls;

🚲 tires;

✏️ erasers;

🧤 rubber gloves;

👢 some boots.

Rubber can be:

• flexible;
• stretchy;
• waterproof;
• grippy.

These properties make rubber useful for many jobs.

==================================================
VISUAL 2 — COMMON MATERIALS
==================================================

Create seven labeled material cards.

🪵 WOOD
Chair or pencil

🔩 METAL
Spoon or key

🧴 PLASTIC
Bottle or toy

🪟 GLASS
Window or jar

📄 PAPER
Book or notebook

👕 FABRIC
Shirt or blanket

🟠 RUBBER
Ball or tire

Caption:

"Different materials are useful for different objects."

==================================================
SECTION 9 — WHAT IS A PROPERTY? 🔍
==================================================

A property is something we can observe or describe about a material.

We can use our senses carefully to learn about materials.

We might ask:

Is it hard or soft?

Is it smooth or rough?

Is it stiff or flexible?

Can we see through it?

Does it soak up water?

Can it stretch?

These observations help us compare materials.

==================================================
SECTION 10 — HARD AND SOFT 🧱🧸
==================================================

Some materials feel hard.

Examples:

🔩 metal;

🪵 wood;

🪟 glass.

Other materials can feel soft.

Examples:

🧸 soft fabric;

🛏️ a blanket;

🧽 foam.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE
--------------------------------------------------

A metal spoon is hard.

A soft blanket is soft.

Hard and soft are properties we can use to describe materials.

==================================================
SECTION 11 — SMOOTH AND ROUGH ✋
==================================================

Some surfaces feel smooth.

Others feel rough.

A glass window may feel smooth.

A rough piece of wood may feel uneven.

Touch can help us notice texture.

Texture means how a surface feels.

⚠️ SAFETY:

Only touch objects that are safe to handle.

Do not touch sharp, hot, or broken materials.

==================================================
SECTION 12 — FLEXIBLE AND STIFF ↪️
==================================================

A flexible material can bend without breaking easily.

A stiff material does not bend easily.

Examples:

A rubber band is flexible.

A metal spoon is usually much stiffer.

Fabric can also be flexible.

Some plastic can bend too.

Different objects need different amounts of flexibility.

==================================================
SECTION 13 — WATERPROOF AND ABSORBENT 💧
==================================================

Some materials resist water.

We call these waterproof or water-resistant materials.

Examples can include:

🧴 some plastics;

🟠 rubber;

🧥 waterproof fabric.

Other materials absorb water.

Absorb means to take in liquid.

Examples:

🧽 sponge;

🧻 paper towel;

some fabrics.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE
--------------------------------------------------

Imagine making an umbrella.

Would paper be a good material?

Probably not.

Paper can absorb water and become weak.

A waterproof material is a better choice.

==================================================
VISUAL 3 — MATERIAL PROPERTIES
==================================================

Create a simple comparison chart:

HARD 🧱
Metal

SOFT 🧸
Fabric

SMOOTH ✋
Glass

ROUGH 🪵
Unfinished wood

FLEXIBLE ↪️
Rubber

WATERPROOF 💧
Plastic

ABSORBENT 🧽
Sponge or paper towel

Caption:

"Properties help us describe and compare materials."

==================================================
SECTION 14 — TRANSPARENT AND OPAQUE 👀
==================================================

Some materials let light pass through.

If we can see through a material clearly, we call it transparent.

Glass used in many windows is transparent.

Other materials block our view.

We can call these opaque.

Wood is usually opaque.

Metal is usually opaque.

Paper is usually opaque.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE
--------------------------------------------------

Why is clear glass useful for a window?

Because we can see through it and light can pass through.

==================================================
SECTION 15 — ONE OBJECT, DIFFERENT MATERIALS 🔄
==================================================

The same type of object can sometimes be made from different materials.

Think about a chair.

A chair can be made from:

🪵 wood;

🔩 metal;

🧴 plastic.

The material may change how the chair feels, looks, weighs, or how long it lasts.

Think about a cup.

A cup may be made from:

🪟 glass;

🧴 plastic;

🔩 metal;

or other safe materials.

This shows us that there can be more than one suitable material for an object.

==================================================
SECTION 16 — ONE OBJECT CAN USE MANY MATERIALS 🧩
==================================================

Some objects are made from several materials.

Think about a bicycle. 🚲

It may have:

🔩 a metal frame;

🟠 rubber tires;

🧴 plastic parts;

🪑 fabric or foam on the seat.

Each material is chosen because it has useful properties.

This is called choosing materials for a purpose.

==================================================
WORKED EXAMPLE — WHAT SHOULD A RAINCOAT BE MADE FROM? 🌧️
==================================================

Imagine we want to make a raincoat.

What property do we need most?

STEP 1:

Think about what a raincoat must do.

It should help keep water away from the person wearing it.

STEP 2:

Compare materials.

Paper:
can absorb water and become weak.

Wood:
hard and uncomfortable to wear.

Glass:
hard and breakable.

Waterproof fabric:
flexible and resists water.

STEP 3:

Choose the material that fits the job.

CONCLUSION:

🧥 A flexible waterproof material is a good choice for a raincoat.

==================================================
GUIDED EXAMPLE — WHAT SHOULD A WINDOW BE MADE FROM? 🪟
==================================================

A window should let us see outside and allow light to pass through.

Which property is useful?

Transparent.

Which material is commonly transparent and suitable for windows?

Glass.

So:

🪟 Glass is useful for many windows because it can be transparent.

==================================================
SECTION 17 — CHOOSING THE RIGHT MATERIAL 🎯
==================================================

We choose materials based on what an object needs to do.

--------------------------------------------------
UMBRELLA ☔
--------------------------------------------------

Useful property:

Waterproof

--------------------------------------------------
BLANKET 🛏️
--------------------------------------------------

Useful property:

Soft

--------------------------------------------------
WINDOW 🪟
--------------------------------------------------

Useful property:

Transparent

--------------------------------------------------
BICYCLE TIRE 🚲
--------------------------------------------------

Useful properties:

Flexible and grippy

--------------------------------------------------
SPOON 🥄
--------------------------------------------------

Useful properties:

Hard and strong

The "best" material depends on the job.

==================================================
SECTION 18 — CHANGING MATERIALS ✂️
==================================================

Materials can sometimes be changed.

Paper can be:

folded;

cut;

torn.

Clay can be:

pressed;

rolled;

shaped.

Fabric can be:

cut;

folded;

sewn.

Metal can be shaped using special tools.

Changing the shape of a material does not always create a new material.

A folded sheet of paper is still paper.

==================================================
SECTION 19 — REUSE ♻️
==================================================

Some objects can be used again instead of being thrown away.

This is called reuse.

Examples:

🫙 A clean jar may be reused for storage.

📦 A box may be reused to hold objects.

🎨 Clean safe materials may be reused for art projects.

Reusing objects can help reduce waste.

Always make sure reused objects are clean and safe.

==================================================
SECTION 20 — RECYCLING ♻️
==================================================

Some materials can be collected and processed so they can be used again.

This is called recycling.

Materials that may be recyclable in some places include:

📄 paper;

🧴 some plastics;

🔩 some metals;

🪟 some glass.

Recycling rules are different in different places.

Always follow local recycling instructions and adult guidance.

For Grade 1, remember:

♻️ Recycling can help turn some used materials into useful materials again.

==================================================
VISUAL 4 — REDUCE, REUSE, RECYCLE
==================================================

Create a simple three-part visual:

REDUCE
Use only what we need.

REUSE
Use safe objects again.

RECYCLE
Sort suitable materials for recycling.

Use simple Grade 1 examples.

Caption:

"We can make careful choices about the materials we use."

==================================================
SECTION 21 — MATERIAL SAFETY ⚠️
==================================================

Science means observing carefully.

It also means staying safe.

Do not:

❌ touch broken glass;

❌ touch sharp metal;

❌ touch very hot objects;

❌ taste unknown materials;

❌ put unknown materials in your mouth.

If an object looks dangerous, ask a trusted adult for help.

ACTIVITY — CHOOSE THE BETTER MATERIAL 🎯
==================================================

You want to make something that keeps rain off your head.

Which is better?

Paper or waterproof material?

Better choice:
Waterproof material 💧

--------------------------------------------------

You want to make a clear window.

Which is better?

Transparent glass or wood?

Better choice:
Transparent glass 🪟

--------------------------------------------------

You want a soft blanket.

Which is better?

Soft fabric or hard metal?

Better choice:
Soft fabric 🛏️

==================================================
COMMON MISTAKES ⚠️
==================================================

MISTAKE 1:

"Every object is made from only one material."

❌ Not true.

Many objects contain several materials.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 2:

"Every plastic object has the same properties."

❌ Not true.

Some plastics are hard.

Others are flexible.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 3:

"Glass is always the best material for everything."

❌ Not true.

Glass is useful for some purposes, but it can break.

Different jobs need different materials.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 4:

"Soft materials are weak and useless."

❌ Not true.

Soft materials are useful for things such as clothing, blankets, cushions, and other objects.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 5:

"Any material can be used safely for any job."

❌ Not true.

Materials are chosen because their properties fit the purpose.

==================================================
QUICK CHECK 🧠
==================================================

1. WHAT MATERIAL IS A METAL SPOON MADE FROM?

Answer:
Metal 🔩

Why?
Metal is hard and strong, making it useful for many utensils.

--------------------------------------------------

2. WHICH PROPERTY IS USEFUL FOR A WINDOW?

Answer:
Transparent 👀

Why?
A transparent material lets us see through it.

--------------------------------------------------

3. WHICH MATERIAL IS OFTEN FLEXIBLE AND USED FOR TIRES?

Answer:
Rubber 🟠

Why?
Rubber can bend and provide grip.

--------------------------------------------------

4. WHY IS PAPER NOT A GOOD MATERIAL FOR AN UMBRELLA?

Answer:
It can absorb water. 💧

Why?
Wet paper can become weak.

--------------------------------------------------

5. CAN ONE OBJECT BE MADE FROM MORE THAN ONE MATERIAL?

Answer:
Yes ✅

Why?
Many objects combine different materials for different jobs.

==================================================
KEY CONCEPT ⭐
==================================================

TITLE:

Different materials have different properties.

BODY:

Objects are made from materials such as wood, metal, plastic, glass, paper, fabric, and rubber.

Materials can be hard, soft, smooth, rough, flexible, waterproof, absorbent, transparent, or opaque.

We choose materials based on what we need an object to do.

==================================================
FINAL RECAP 🌟
==================================================

Remember:

🪵 Wood is used for many strong objects.

🔩 Metal is often hard and strong.

🧴 Plastic can be light, waterproof, hard, or flexible.

🪟 Glass can be transparent but can break.

📄 Paper is light and easy to fold.

👕 Fabric can be soft and flexible.

🟠 Rubber can be flexible and grippy.

🔎 Properties help us compare materials.

🎯 We choose materials based on their purpose.

♻️ Some objects and materials can be reused or recycled.

⚠️ Always handle materials safely.

==================================================
QUIZ ACCURACY REQUIREMENTS
==================================================

Avoid questions that falsely suggest every material has only one property.

BAD:

"Plastic is always flexible."

This is false because different plastics have different properties.

BETTER:

"Which material can be made waterproof and is often used for bottles?"

Possible correct answer:
Plastic

Avoid overly broad claims such as:

"Metal is always shiny."

"Glass is always clear."

"Wood is always rough."

Instead use wording such as:

"Many metals are strong."

"Clear glass can be transparent."

"Some wood feels rough."

==================================================
MATERIAL-PURPOSE QUESTIONS
==================================================

When asking which material is suitable for an object, make sure the property being tested is stated clearly.

Example:

"You want to make a window that lets you see outside. Which material is the best choice?"

A. Soft fabric
B. Clear glass
C. Paper
D. Wood

Correct:
Clear glass

Reason:
It is transparent.

Another example:

"You want to make a raincoat. Which property is most useful?"

A. Absorbent
B. Waterproof
C. Breakable
D. Rough

Correct:
Waterproof
